hero-copy: Pin Context keeps task-related files within reach. Pin or unpin files directly from the VS Code Explorer, switch between focused contexts, and transfer context sets with JSON import and export.
feature-1-title: Pin control where you need it
feature-1-desc: Pin or unpin open tabs, toggle the active file’s pin state, or use the Explorer context menu without opening the file first.
feature-2-desc: Group files by task, feature, or workflow. Save a set and restore it when you return.
feature-3-desc: Use keyboard shortcuts, the Command Palette, and Quick Picks to navigate your workspace with less friction.
feature-4-desc: Return to recently used contexts from a timeline grouped by day.
feature-5-desc: Manage pinned files, named contexts, and recent history from the Pin Context sidebar.
feature-6-desc: Batch limits, safe URI validation, and resilient persistence help keep workflows predictable.
cmd-1-desc: Pin the active editor file or the file selected in Explorer.
cmd-2-desc: Unpin the active editor file or the file selected in Explorer.
cmd-3-desc: Toggle pinning for the active editor file or the file selected in Explorer.
cmd-4-desc: Switch to another task context in one step.
workflow-title: A workflow that stays out of your way
step-1: Pin task-related files from the editor or the Explorer context menu.
step-2: Save the pinned set as a named context for the task.
step-3: Switch contexts as you move between features or Git branches.
step-4: Export context sets to JSON to move them between workspaces or share them with your team.
step-5: Use Quick Open and the context timeline to return to recent work.
footer-text: Built for developers who move fast.
support-subtitle: Help keep development active and evolving.
wallet-info-eth: send only via Ethereum / ERC20 network
cmp-vscode-1: Open tabs do not form named task contexts
cmp-vscode-2: File sets must be rebuilt manually
cmp-vscode-4: No built-in JSON transfer for Pin Context sets
cmp-vscode-6: No Pin Context metadata tools for MCP agents
cmp-vscode-7: No context-change approval flow for this feature
cmp-pin-1: Named contexts for tasks and workflows
cmp-pin-2: Pin or unpin files directly in Explorer
cmp-pin-5: Portable, validated JSON import and export
cmp-pin-7: MCP and public API for compatible AI agents
analytics-copy: With your consent, Google Analytics receives page views and interaction events, such as feature clicks and language or platform selection, plus approximate engagement time. Query strings and URL fragments are removed. Analytics remains off unless you opt in.
feature-7-desc: Right-click a file to pin or unpin it. The available action matches the file’s current state.
feature-8-desc: Export contexts to JSON and import them elsewhere. Imported data is validated, and contexts are merged by name.
feature-9-desc: Share context metadata with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and compatible MCP clients. Changes require your approval.
explorer-eyebrow: A QUICK ACTION, RIGHT WHERE YOU NEED IT
explorer-intro: You no longer need to open a file first. Right-click a file in the Explorer tree: unpinned files show “Pin File”, while pinned files show “Unpin File”. Multi-selection is supported.
explorer-step-1-desc: Right-click a file in the Explorer sidebar, even if it is not open in an editor.
explorer-step-2-desc: The menu offers the action that matches the selected file’s current pin state.
explorer-step-3-desc: Save the resulting set as a context, then switch back to it when you return to the task.
explorer-menu-caption: Example of the file action. The menu changes to “Unpin File” once the file is pinned.
demo-ready: Try switching contexts, pinning a file, or exporting JSON.
demo-caption: A small interactive preview — changes stay in this page.
demo-context-main-desc: Shared workspace files and extension entry points.
demo-context-search-desc: Files related to Quick Open and keyboard navigation.
demo-context-api-desc: A context for tasks involving data storage and state persistence.
demo-contexts-desc: Switch contexts to see a different set of pinned files.
demo-history-desc: Jump back into a context you used earlier.
demo-empty-pins: No pinned files match this filter.
demo-empty-available: No other sample files are available to pin.
demo-empty-history: No recent contexts match this filter.
agents-title: Connect your AI agent to the active context
agents-intro: Pin Context exposes the active VS Code context through a public extension API and MCP. Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and other compatible agents can inspect contexts and pinned files. Any changes require your approval.
agent-flow-aria: Interactive diagram of how Pin Context connects AI agents
agent-flow-stage-aria: Select a node to learn about that step in the context flow
agent-flow-context-desc: Pin Context exposes context metadata and pinned-file paths. The agent reads file contents using its own workspace tools.
agent-flow-mcp-desc: MCP makes Pin Context tools available to compatible clients. Read operations inspect state; write operations require approval.
agent-flow-claude-desc: Claude Code can read the context and pinned-file list, then use its own tools to inspect project files.
agent-flow-codex-desc: Codex uses the same MCP tool set. Context changes are gated by the extension approval flow.
agents-benefit-1-desc: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, VS Code Chat, and other MCP clients use the same tools to work with contexts.
agents-benefit-2-desc: Agents can inspect the active context and its pinned-file list. They read file contents through their own workspace tools.
agents-benefit-3-desc: Changing contexts or pinned files requires approval. If you cancel, the state remains unchanged.
agents-vscode-title: Use Pin Context tools in VS Code Chat
agents-vscode-step-1: Open VS Code Chat, then open the tool picker.
agents-vscode-step-2: Find Pin Context and enable its tools for the current chat.
agents-vscode-step-3: Try the read-only test prompt below. VS Code shows its own confirmation dialog for MCP tools that change state.
agents-vscode-note: Read-only operations do not change extension state. VS Code asks for approval before running an MCP tool that changes state; review the requested action before approving it.
agents-other-step-1: Ensure Pin Context is active in the VS Code workspace you want to expose.
agents-other-step-2: Run “Pin Context: Copy MCP Client Configuration”, then copy the mcpServers.pin-context object from the generated JSON.
agents-other-step-3: Add the entry to the client’s stdio MCP configuration. Keep the command, argument order, and environment variables unchanged.
agents-other-note: The client starts a local Node.js process that forwards requests to the active extension. Node.js must be available to the client; set its absolute path if needed. Do not share the generated bridge configuration with others because it contains access credentials.
agents-test-title: Test tool discovery without making changes
agents-test-prompt: Use the Pin Context MCP tools to report the active context, list available contexts, and list pinned files. Do not switch contexts or change any pins.
agents-copy-failed: Clipboard access is unavailable. Select and copy the prompt manually.
agents-safety-note: Pin Context returns context metadata and file paths, not file contents. The agent reads file contents through its own workspace tools. Changes to contexts or pinned files require approval.
agents-source-build-suffix: to build and install the extension with MCP support. Skip these steps if you installed a Marketplace build that already includes MCP support.
agents-setup-subtitle: Choose a client to see setup steps for its configuration format.
agents-claude-title: Connect Claude Code to the active VS Code workspace
agents-claude-step-1: Open the target project in VS Code, wait for Pin Context to activate, then run “Pin Context: Copy MCP Client Configuration”.
agents-claude-step-2: Copy the mcpServers.pin-context object from the generated JSON, without the outer mcpServers object.
agents-claude-step-3: Run the command below in a terminal, replacing the placeholder with the exact JSON object from the generated configuration:
agents-claude-step-4: Run claude mcp list, then use /mcp inside Claude Code to confirm that the server is connected.
agents-claude-note: The generated bridge configuration is tied to the current VS Code extension session. Keep that workspace open. If the connection stops working after VS Code reloads, copy the configuration again and update the Claude Code server entry.
agents-status-claude: Verify the connection with /mcp in Claude Code.
agents-codex-title: Connect Pin Context to Codex CLI or its IDE extension
agents-codex-step-1: Open the target project in VS Code, wait for Pin Context to activate, and run “Pin Context: Copy MCP Client Configuration”.
agents-codex-step-2: Open ~/.codex/config.toml and add the server table below. Copy the exact command, args, and PIN_CONTEXT_VERSION values from the generated JSON.
agents-codex-step-3: Replace each placeholder with the corresponding value from the generated configuration. Keep the argument order unchanged.
agents-codex-step-4: Run codex mcp list. In the Codex TUI, you can also run /mcp to inspect the connection.
agents-codex-note: Codex CLI and its IDE extension use the same user-level MCP configuration. Keep the VS Code workspace connected to Pin Context open. If Node.js is not on the client’s PATH, set command to its absolute path: use which node on macOS/Linux or where node on Windows.
agents-other-step-4: Restart the client or reconnect to the MCP server, then confirm that the Pin Context tools appear in the tool list.
site-description: Pin Context for VS Code: organize task contexts, pin files from Explorer, and let AI agents access context metadata safely through MCP.
